written: 2026-11-21, after SeedLM-26, before either SeedLM-27 coder was trained
theory: Every coder's held-out teacher and real-task scores peak about 30 minutes into training while synthetic scores keep rising (SeedLM-8): the few thousand written descriptions are repeated dozens of times and memorized. In SeedLM-26, 400 more steps on repeated original wordings cost about 3 held-out teacher tasks and the same steps on paraphrases cost none. If memorizing the wording is what stops learning, reading each repeated task in other words should let held-out scores keep rising after 30 minutes
arms: two post-coders from scratch, s12-a1's arguments with 80 minutes instead of 40, seed 1, a checkpoint every 20 minutes (--save-every 20): s27-c, and s27-p with --paraphrases (the 1,200 paraphrased training tasks also appear in their two other wordings inside the real and teacher shares; data/seedlm/paraphrase/). Nothing else runs while they train
measure: at 20, 40, 60 and 80 minutes, the first program at beam width 32 that reproduces the visible example is right on every case (SeedLM-15's cache), on the held-out teacher tasks (139) and the development fifth (94)
primary_measure: held-out teacher tasks: the mean over the 60- and 80-minute checkpoints minus the mean over the 20- and 40-minute checkpoints, s27-p minus s27-c. Supported if at least +4; not supported if at most 0; inconclusive otherwise
secondary_measures: the same contrast on the development fifth
each arm's best checkpoint on each set (reported, not chosen)
caveat: one seed per arm: 40-minute seeds of one setting differ by 3 to 6 held-out teacher tasks (SeedLM-12)
choice: diagnostic; the system's adoption rule is unchanged

outcome.primary: held-out teacher tasks, late minus early checkpoints (means of 60 and 80 minutes against 20 and 40): s27-c +3.0, s27-p +2.5; s27-p minus s27-c -0.5, at most 0: not supported
secondary: development fifth, the same contrast: s27-c -3.0, s27-p +4.5; difference +7.5 (one seed per arm)
best checkpoints: teacher 53 for both; development 61 (s27-p at 80 minutes) against 61 (s27-c at 40)
outcome.reported: the system with each 80-minute coder on the development fifth (scripts/seedlm4_tasks.py holdout): best 68 for both (s27-p: pyx_tie 68, pyx_override 67; s27-c: pyx_tie_fill 68, pyx_override 67), against 69 with s5-var. s27-p alone 61, its answers mostly the engine's own (against the engine it fixes 3 and breaks 7)
outcome.note: the checkpoints at 20 to 60 minutes are taken mid-schedule (the learning rate decays over the whole 80 minutes), so they are lower than finished 40-minute runs (s12-a1: teacher 59) and are compared only between the two arms
outcome.reading: Paraphrases did not keep the held-out teacher score rising: both 80-minute coders end near 52, below every finished 40-minute coder. On the real development tasks the paraphrase coder rose steadily to 61 while the control wandered, which fits its 525 paraphrased real tasks, but with one seed this is a lead, not a finding, and in the system it changed nothing
